commit: the branch head that contains this file (models fitted at d86f683; evaluation plan committed at d6f4767; checkpoints committed at 9f7f832)

requirements.notes: E1 alone fits three domains on real data: content_selection (content_consumption, content_consumption_feed, news_click), watch_duration, browsing_frequency (return_daily, session_rate). E2's models add domains when merged.

content_consumption_fitted is true (content_consumption@1, fitted and evaluated under KuaiRand random exposure). randomized_commercial_response_fitted is computed from the registry and becomes true when E2's randomised commercial-response model is registered (domain advertising_response or purchase_behavior, identification randomized_controlled_trial). Until then the F.2 test fails, and because the checker requires every test of test_gate_F.py to pass, no F requirement can verify before the merge.

six held-out reports (JSON + Markdown) on held-out users and later periods; the gate test recomputes each E1 model's held-out primary metric from the verified data and the saved checkpoint with registry.load.
each model is compared with two simple baselines on the same held-out split, with a user-cluster bootstrap interval of the difference; all six learned models beat their best baseline.
ECE (15 bins), Brier and reliability tables; PIT uniformity and interval coverage for watch time; count calibration by predicted decile for sessions.
six checkpoints (NumPy npz without pickle, 0.4 KB to 312 KB) with SHA-256 in the model cards; load verifies hashes; tampering is detected (tested).

two datasets (kuairand_pure, mind_small) with SHA-256 per file (and per extracted file), schema validation, licence and full provenance; the criterion asks for 3, which E2's datasets supply after merging (register them with datasets.register from a module named calibration/datasets_<x>.py, which datasets() imports automatically).
each card and report states what the simulator may and may not infer: population, platform, period, value ranges, identification, scale mapping.
a model counts only if it cites a registered, checksummed, non-synthetic dataset; synthetic_only_domains = 0.

26 important mechanisms today (7 grounded by E1 models, 19 behavioural 4.0 mechanisms), all with complete records. Important mechanisms are computed, so every kernel module that a v5 behaviour package (population, social, commerce, innovation, multiagent, civ, domains, semantic) registers needs a FIDELITY_REGISTER.md row naming it in the module column, or SP-5.4 fails.

the plan was committed (d6f4767) before any fit; fitlib refuses to fit with an uncommitted or modified plan; the test checks the plan's hash at the recorded commit, commit order (plan before fit and before the checkpoint commit), the prespecified primary/secondary metrics and candidates, and that no kept model is worse than a simple baseline (worse_model_kept = 0).

limitations: Two platforms, two periods, two selected samples: Kuaishou (China) April-May 2022 and Microsoft News (US) November 2019; each card's limits says what may and may not be inferred.
Only content_consumption rests on randomised exposure; its feature effects are still associations among randomly shown items. All other models are observational.

KuaiRand-Pure logs only pool-video interactions, so absolute activity is undercounted; scale-dependent inputs must be quantile-mapped (feature_quantiles in each card). The random-insertion rate rose during the period, visible as upward drift in held-out return and session levels (session count calibration error 0.43).
Item ages in KuaiRand cover 0-30 days and are confounded with calendar time (all pool videos uploaded 2022-04-09..11).
The watch model is pooled over both logs; on recommender-selected exposures alone it under-predicts long watches (PIT KS 0.084).

MIND-small was downloaded from the ungated Hugging Face mirror huyva/MIND-small (pinned revision) because the official copy is gated behind a licence click-through and no credential is configured; files match the official statistics.
No separate repeat-consumption model: re-consumption is too rare in KuaiRand-Pure (145 standard and 8 random-exposure rows); it is an input of the choice models.
MIND text affinity uses TF-IDF + truncated SVD computed here, not the semantic workstream's neural encoders.
The NumPy tree predictor costs about 40 microseconds per row for 400 trees; batch calls.
integration_notes: Merge (do not squash) this branch: SP-5.5 checks that the plan commit d6f4767 precedes the checkpoint commit and is contained in the fit commit d86f683; a squash would remove those commits from history and fail the test.

E2 unification: E2's models count in gate F once each is saved with crucible.calibration.registry.save_model into docs/v5/calibration/models/<name>/ with domain in registry.DOMAINS (advertising_response or purchase_behavior for commercial response), provenance.identification in registry.IDENTIFICATION (randomized_controlled_trial for Criteo uplift), provenance.datasets naming datasets registered via crucible.calibration.datasets.register (put the registration in calibration/datasets_<x>.py so datasets() imports it), provenance.evaluation_plan {path, sha256, commit} of a plan committed before the fit (fitlib.plan_record does this), a selection record with baselines and candidates (fitlib.select), and a report with heldout_splits, splits (rows/users), baseline_comparison, calibration and extrapolation_limits (fitlib.finish writes all of this). A registry_e2.py with its own datasets()/load() should be folded into these calls; audit.py reads only the on-disk cards.

Population (B) and social (C): load models with crucible.calibration.load('<name>@1'); feature definitions and simulator mappings are in each card's feature_map and in docs/v5/components/E1.md. Use content_consumption (randomised exposure) as the individual's keep-watching/choice rule; content_consumption_feed is an observational engagement target for a learned recommender, not a choice rule.

SP-5.4 computes important mechanisms from the code: every kernel module registered from crucible.population/social/commerce/innovation/multiagent/civ/domains/semantic must be named in the module column of a docs/v5/FIDELITY_REGISTER.md row (category, evidence with dataset and year for empirical rows, held-out result, limits).

Gate F needs the datasets under $CRUCIBLE_DATA (default /workspace/data/crucible; acquire downloads and verifies them if absent, about 450 MB for E1) and takes about 5 minutes: run it through slots with --cpu 2.

Orchestrator bug noticed (not changed): crucible/acceptance/v5/evidence.py git() strips the whole porcelain output, so the first status line loses its leading space and its path loses the first character (seen as 'rucible/docs/v5/FIDELITY_REGISTER.md' in dirty_paths); a modified tracked evidence file listed first would then be reported as a dirty non-evidence path.
Running the v5 acceptance checker tests rewrites docs/v5/evidence/checker_report.json in the working tree; it was restored, not committed.
pyproject.toml gains an optional extra v5-calibration (scikit-learn, scipy, pandas, torch), all already installed in /venv/main; nothing was installed.
